description.p: Reyva is a lightweight Chromium-based browser that keeps nothing by default. Tabs, history, cookies and site data live in memory and are gone when you close it. No account, no sync, no telemetry.

ul.li: Shields: built-in tracker and ad blocking, with per-site exceptions
HTTPS upgrade, tracking-parameter stripping and fingerprinting protection
Optional saved passwords, stored in your system keyring
Bookmarks with folders, and import from other browsers
Reader mode, find in page and a download manager
Low Memory Mode, which suspends background tabs you are not using

description.p: With "Ask where to save each file" on, a download goes straight into the folder you pick, including USB sticks and other drives, instead of filling Downloads first.
File names that USB sticks refuse (like "Game: Title") are fixed automatically.
The Downloads list has a Clear button and a remove button on each finished download; the files stay.
On ReyOS, Reyva's colors match grey and softer Looks too: Graphite is grey instead of blue-purple, Forest is softer.
Downloads can go anywhere: turn on "Ask where to save each file" in Settings to pick a folder for each download.
Redesigned Settings, Downloads, Bookmarks, Passwords and Web Apps windows; bookmark imports keep their folders.
On ReyOS, Reyva follows the Look you pick in Control Center instead of always being copper.
Show in Folder and Open Downloads Folder in the downloads list open the file manager again, with the downloaded file selected.
Print preview like other browsers: see the pages before printing, and pick the printer, pages, copies, layout, paper size, color and two-sided printing, or save as PDF.
Settings redesigned: shows the Reyva version, has an on/off switch for Shields, and now remembers your search engine.
"Print to File (PDF)" in the print dialog now suggests a file name in Downloads instead of an empty one.
Printing works: Print (Ctrl+P) and Save Page as PDF in the menu, and the print buttons on web pages and in the PDF viewer now open the print dialog.
Videos show their picture again on Intel graphics: Reyva now decodes video on the CPU, because frames decoded by the GPU were lost before they reached the screen.
Video fullscreen works: a player's fullscreen button now fills the screen and hides the toolbars. Press Esc to leave it.
Install any site as an app: it gets its own window and its own entry in your app menu, through your desktop's own confirmation dialog.
